answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Each collapsed cluster gets one haven weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. The sonnet report exposes the merge explicitly at each thread. A 192 account operation therefore ties up 39 million dollars of idle capital. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
